issues.title: Packing slips just in time, one email per fulfillment group

milestone.title: Next release
milestone.description: The next production release. Planning rules: north-foster-farm/north-foster-farm#527.

issues.body:
## Status (2026-11-20)

James asked for this in chat on 2026-11-20. Not started; tests first. Wording marked "draft" goes to James before it ships.

## What happens today

The packing slips are built and mailed by `netlify/functions/lib/packing.mjs`, run by the scheduled job in `netlify/functions/lib/jobs.mjs`. Production sends two packets a day, each one email with one PDF for every kind of fulfillment together:

- **3:00 PM** (#515, "Send every slip for tomorrow at 3 PM the day before"): every slip for tomorrow, plus each new, changed or cancelled order for later days. Subject: "Packing slips for tomorrow, {day}: {counts}".
- **6:00 AM**: what came in or changed after the 3 PM packet. On Sunday, a clean slip for every order of the coming week as well. On a quiet day, an email saying there is nothing to print.
- All day: an order due today that changes after it was printed is mailed at once as "Changed after printing".

So the farm gets slips for later days early, a weekly batch on Sunday, and one email whose attachment names it has to scan to see what is in it.

## Spec

**Just in time, one rule for every way:** on-farm pickup, pickup days (the drop site, each market, each pop-up) and delivery.

1. **3:00 PM the day before:** the slips for tomorrow's orders, and only tomorrow's. No slips for later days, and no weekly Sunday batch.
2. **6:00 AM the day of:** the slips for today's orders that came in, changed or were cancelled after the 3 PM packet (late orders). Nothing else.
3. **One email per fulfillment group,** each with its own PDF holding only that group's slips (and its own pick list): on-farm pickup; each pickup-day place and occasion (the drop site, each market, each pop-up, separately); delivery. A group with nothing to print gets no email.
4. **Subjects easy to read in an inbox:** `{place} packing slips for {Weekday} {M/D}`, with no year. James's examples: "North Scituate drop site packing slips for Saturday 11/21", "Pawtucket Thanksgiving Prep packing slips for Saturday 11/21". For the others, draft: "On-farm pickup packing slips for Saturday 11/21", "Delivery packing slips for Wednesday 11/25". The place reads the way the farm names it: the town of the place's location and the occasion's name, from `data/locations.json` and `data/series.json` (the drop site's town is North Scituate). Late slips at 6 AM, draft: "Late: North Scituate drop site packing slips for Saturday 11/21".
5. **A day with nothing at all to print** sends one short email at 3 PM, draft "No packing slips for Saturday 11/21", so silence never stands for a failure. Nothing goes at 6 AM when nothing is late.
6. **Unchanged:** "Changed after printing" during the day; the 6 PM "tomorrow" summary and the 8 AM morning report; what a slip shows; what counts as printed (`packing/printed/`), so a reprint still comes from comparing with what was printed; the healthcheck ping (once per run, failing if any group's email could not be built or sent).
7. The docs and the comments at the top of `lib/packing.mjs` and `lib/jobs.mjs` say what is true now, dated.

## Done when

- [ ] At 3 PM, each fulfillment group with orders tomorrow gets its own email and PDF with exactly that group's slips for tomorrow, and nothing for later days
- [ ] At 6 AM, each group with orders for today that arrived, changed or were cancelled after the 3 PM packet gets its own email with exactly those, and a group with nothing late gets none
- [ ] There is no weekly Sunday batch
- [ ] Each subject reads `{place} packing slips for {Weekday} {M/D}`, as in James's examples, and late ones are marked as late
- [ ] A day with nothing to print sends the one "no packing slips" email at 3 PM
- [ ] "Changed after printing", the printed records, the summaries and the healthcheck behave as before
- [ ] `communications` has reviewed the subjects and James has approved the drafts on the pull request

issues.body:
## Status (2026-11-20)

James decided in chat on 2026-11-20, after the second release shipped on two attempts of one full run: "We should be automatically retry failing e2e tests going forward." Not started; tests first.

He also set the release rule that day, recorded on #667: ship when every test has passed across the attempts on one commit, and none of the failures points to a problem in the site's own code.

James, in chat, later on 2026-11-20: "Flaky tests don't need to be fixed for the same release. I don't want flaky tests to block releases. They should be filed for fix imminently after. And we need to update the promote command so that we can, in circumstances where we deliberately want to ship with failing tests on staging, that should be doable through the promote command." The coordinator proposes that the deliberate override below also answer #656 (a recorded exemption for bot-challenge failures) finding 4 (the approver field binds nothing), by binding to the release pull request he labels; that finding is still his to decide.

## What happens

The full staging run (`e2e-staging.yml`) runs with Playwright retries off (#502 and the staging rules in `docs/cloud-lanes.md`), so one transport stall, a connection reset or a Netlify bot challenge on any of about 1,250 tests fails the whole run. Each rerun of the run costs about 40 minutes and Netlify function time (#519). The second release needed eight attempts across three commits; the hotfix five. Almost every failure passed on the next attempt.

## Spec

- Failing tests are retried automatically, within the same run, on staging full runs and on the local-build runs (`e2e.yml`, `e2e-run.yml`). A retry count of 2 is the starting point; say why if you choose another.
- A test that fails and then passes on a retry is reported as flaky, by name, in the run's summary and in the verdict `bin/nff e2e` prints, so a flaky test is seen and can be fixed, never hidden.
- `bin/nff promote main` accepts a full staging run in which every test passed, on its first try or on a retry, and names each flaky test it accepted, as it names exemptions today. A test that fails every try still fails the run.
- The retries do not fire twice for anything that changes staging state in a way a retry cannot repeat (a single-use token, a payment): say which specs need it and how they are guarded (Playwright's `retries: 0` per describe, or a fresh setup per try).
- A flaky test never blocks a release. Each flaky test a run reports is filed as an issue (or added to its open one) in the Next release milestone, named and linked from the run, so it is fixed right after the release, not before it.
- **A deliberate override:** `bin/nff promote main` can ship a commit whose full staging run has failing tests when James chooses to. The failing tests and the reason are listed on the release pull request (the one he labels LGTM), the promote command reads them from there, refuses any failure not listed, and logs what it shipped past. It replaces neither the LGTM label nor the green checks.
- `docs/cloud-lanes.md` and any rule that says retries are off say what is true now, dated.

## Done when

- [ ] A test agent's test shows `bin/nff promote main` accepts a run whose only failures passed on a retry, names them as flaky, and still refuses a run with a test that failed every try
- [ ] A test agent's test shows `bin/nff promote main` ships a run with failing tests only when each failure is listed with a reason on the release pull request it reads, refuses one that is not listed, and logs what it shipped past
- [ ] A flaky test in a run is filed as an issue in the Next release milestone, or added to its open one
- [ ] `bin/nff e2e`'s verdict names a test that passed on a retry as flaky
- [ ] The workflows run with retries on, and the specs that must not repeat are guarded
- [ ] The docs and rules say retries are on

issues.body:
## Status (2026-11-19)

Shipped to production on 2026-11-19 in #603 (`main` 1aad8a04). Left: James's look at the Membership tab on the real page, as #614 revised it (host and member, phone and desktop). It was step 2 of his staging look on #603 (2026-11-19), after which he said to release; if that covered it, this closes. Production and staging (one landing ahead) both serve it.

As of 2026-11-18, landed: Landed through PR #604: five commits on `next`, head e146cd21. On staging at e146cd21 (deploy confirmed by version.json, 2026-11-18). James accepted the build from its screenshots with three changes, all made. The criteria tests were written by a separate test lane (db8294d2); the implementer changed no expectation (checked by diff before landing). Left: James's look at the real page on staging, on his phone and desktop, asked on the release PR #603.

## Changes from James's review of the build (2026-11-18)

- **A pickup has happened at the end of its window.** A closed round stays on the tab until its pickup window ends (8:30 to 9:00 AM: until 9:00).
- **One column on medium screens.** The rounds stack below `lg` (992 px) and sit side by side from `lg` up: `col-12 col-lg-6`. At 768 px they are stacked. This replaces the build's `col-md-6`.
- **The closed line** reads "Next pickup is Sunday, Nov 22" (the pickup's date), not "Pickup is ...". The pill stays "Closed".
- Accepted as built: the headings "Pickups" and "Invite members", the "Order now" button, the account head in one column below 768 px, the host's Download QR code as an outline button, the member's hidden download button, and "Opens on" giving the day after the close.

## James's decisions (2026-11-18, his words where quoted)

"I like mockup C, but those dates are going to encounter the badge and wrap in an awkward way. the badges themselves being on the far right edge is also a little unusual... I would like to see some hierarchy within the rounds too."

His sketch of a round (in the first comment):

> **Saturday, Nov 21** · 10:00 – 11:00 AM
> ( Open ) Closes at 11:59 PM on Sat, Nov 20
>
> **Saturday, Nov 21** · 10:00 – 11:00 AM
> ( Next ) Opens on Sun, Nov 22

- "there should probably be a button that links to the order page."
- "This layout should also be a flex layout, so that the current and next round sit side-by-side unless they need to wrap. Bootstrap should handle this pretty easily with `col col-lg-6`."
- "no need to include any 'this round runs every X'."
- "the current member page has the same header spacing issues we fixed recently" (#579, item 1: section headings sat flush under what came before).
- The member code: "the member ID code does nothing yet, and we can't look it up. At a market, we would manually add the customer's name by searching in Square on the POS app. So right now, don't show this code, don't show a 'print a keytag' button. The QR code itself should have a white opacity over it and 'Coming soon' overlaid in a badge." The heading "should be something else like 'Membership QR code'", and the text below it:

> Coming soon: scan your code when you make a purchase in person (like at a farmers market), and your membership benefits will apply automatically. **In the meantime, let us know you are a member at checkout, and we'll look up your membership by name or email.**

## Spec

**The group (direction C).** The group's name at the account email's size (1.25rem bold) with its address as one small gray line under it. Under it, sections at the page's usual section heading: Pickups, then for a host Invite members (the QR code and join link) and Members, and for a member Membership QR code and Leave the group. See #599's direction C mock-ups for the frame.

**A round.** Two lines, as in James's sketch:

1. The pickup: the date bold (weekday in full, month short: "Sunday, Nov 22"), a middle dot, then the pickup window at regular weight ("8:30 – 9:00 AM"). The date and the window each stay whole; if the line must wrap, it breaks at the dot.
2. Under it, smaller and gray: a status pill at the start of the line (never at the right edge), then the deadline. Open: "Closes at 11:59 PM on Sat, Nov 21". Next: "Opens on Sun, Nov 22". The pill and its sentence wrap as ordinary text.

The pill words Open and Next are James's. The sentences follow his sketch; treat their exact wording as his draft to confirm.

**Side by side.** The current and the next round sit side by side when there is room and stack when there isn't: Bootstrap's grid, `col-12 col-lg-6`, inside a row, within `check:grid`'s rules. Say exactly which classes you used and show 390, 768 and 1280 px.

**Order button.** A button that links to the order page, with the open round. Draft label: "Order now". A member following it should land on the order page with the group's pickup and prices available, as the group's link does today. No button on a round that is not open.

**Gone:** the "Rounds run every 2 weeks" line and the Rounds row; the This round and Next round subheadings and the label column from #597 (and its subgrid styles); the group's name repeated in the address.

**Between the close and the pickup (#600).** Check what the data gives after a round closes and before its pickup. If that pickup would vanish from the tab, keep it as a round with its own pill ("Closed") and the line "Next pickup is Sunday, Nov 22" (James, 2026-11-18), ahead of the open round. Fix the data in this branch under #600.

**Member: Membership QR code.** Heading "Membership QR code". James's paragraph above, exactly, second sentence bold. The QR image stays, under a white translucent overlay with a "Coming soon" badge centered on it; give the image an accessible name that says it is not in use yet. Hide the code text (NFM-...), the line about reading the letters aloud, and the "Print a key tag" button. The coordinator's reading, for James to overrule: "Download QR code" is hidden too, since the code does nothing yet. Remove nothing from the server or the CLI; this is display only, easy to turn back on.

**Section heading spacing, member view.** Every section heading on the Membership tab, in both views, has the space above it that #579 gave the host's headings.

**No-break spaces.** None, anywhere (#598): build text with ordinary spaces and `text-nowrap` spans through the `keep-together` helper.

## Done when

- [x] Host and member views match the spec at 390, 768 and 1280 px, in Chromium and WebKit; screenshots of each posted here before landing.
- [x] A round's date and window never break inside themselves, and the pill sits at the start of the second line.
- [x] Two rounds sit side by side from 992 px and stack below it (768 px included); one round alone looks right too.
- [x] The order button reaches the order page with the group applied.
- [x] The member view shows the QR code under the overlay and badge, James's paragraph, and no code text, key tag or download button.
- [x] #600's three moments are covered by a test.
- [x] Unit tests and `e2e/membership.spec.mjs` updated; the gap spec passes; a production build keeps every new class.
- [x] Lint, tests and build green.
- [ ] James approves the screenshots (done, 2026-11-18), then the page on staging (asked on #603).
